name: Highland Trail 550
distance_note: about 550 miles (885 km); recent GPX versions run roughly 890–912 km
summary: A 550-mile self-supported mountain bike loop from Tyndrum through the remote Scottish Highlands, mixing singletrack, dirt roads and quiet tarmac, with plenty of hike-a-bike. It's one of the toughest bikepacking routes in the UK.
facts: The Highland Trail is a self-supported mountain bike route of 550 miles (885 km) with over 16,000 m of climbing, starting from Tyndrum.
Alan Goldsmith first conceived it as a training route for the Colorado Trail Race, and it grew into one of the toughest self-supported off-road time trials in the world.
Most riders in the mass start or time-trial format finish in 4-8 days. The 'summer version' touring route suggests 40-50 miles a day over 11-14 days.
The majority of the route is on good trails and quiet roads, but it includes some boggy and very technical sections.
notes: Expect hike-a-bike on the most spectacular sections, notably the Fisherfield crossing and the Achnashellach/Torridon area. Weather is changeable, so carry proper wet and cold gear.
Tyndrum is reachable by train from Glasgow, which takes a few hours. Bike space is limited, so reserve ahead.
days_hint: 4-8 days for fast riders; 11-14 days as a touring trip
